comments.author: @remaguire
comments.text:
Here is what John Wesley Powell, the man who led the expedition on the Colorado River in the late 1860s, said about water in the West.

“I tell you, gentlemen, you are piling up a heritage of conflict and litigation over water rights, for there is not enough water to supply the land.”

- John Wesley Powell, October 1893

Look up what Powell said about this issue. He warned us about this 133 years ago!!! But we have not (and still don’t) listen. He is worth reading…and listening to.

This part of the USA was not meant for the population we have now. 

By the way, I am a volunteer on Lake Mead driving small boats on safety patrols. So, I pay pretty close attention to this issue. I noticed you mixed and matched video clips. Some from a couple of years ago. Since that time, the lake recovered from the drop in water levels because of a larger than normal snowpack in Colorado. Fast forward to today and we have the opposite situation. Smaller snowpack which is causing probably the biggest crisis in the lake’s history. My point is to separate out the two periods in the interest of accuracy. There is more than enough BS out there about the problem and potential solutions.
